problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-3,-1]\times [-4,-1]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+xy+{y}^{2}-12 \\ {x}^{3}+x-y\end{aligned}].
$$

Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process that starts at ${x}_{0}=[-1,\,-1]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[-1.4,\,-3.6]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).

feedback.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a zero of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-2,2]\times [0,2]⊆{R}^{2},$ where

$$
f(x,y)=[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{3}-xy-4 \\ {x}^{4}-2xy+{y}^{2}-5\end{aligned}].
$$

Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process that starts at ${x}_{0}=[0,\,1]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[-1.5,\,1.5]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).

| ${x}_{2}\,≈[$ | $-1.198$ | $]$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| {{field-1}} |  |  |
feedback.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of finding the zeros of a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to {R}^{n}$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{J}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}f({x}_{n}),
$$

where ${J}_{f}({x}_{n})$ is the Jacobian of $f$ evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the Jacobian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{J}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{3}-xy-4) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{3}-xy-4) \\ \frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{4}-2xy+{y}^{2}-5) & \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{4}-2xy+{y}^{2}-5)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2x-y & 3{y}^{2}-x \\ 4{x}^{3}-2y & -2x+2y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}2x-y & 3{y}^{2}-x \\ 4{x}^{3}-2y & -2x+2y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{3}-xy-4 \\ {x}^{4}-2xy+{y}^{2}-5\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{[\begin{aligned}2x-y & 3{y}^{2}-x \\ 4{x}^{3}-2y & -2x+2y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}+{y}^{3}-xy-4 \\ {x}^{4}-2xy+{y}^{2}-5\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1.5 \\ 1.5\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}2(-1.5)-1.5 & 3(1.5)^{2}-(-1.5) \\ 4(-1.5)^{3}-2(1.5) & -2(-1.5)+2(1.5)\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}(-1.5)^{2}+{1.5}^{3}-(-1.5)\cdot 1.5-4 \\ (-1.5)^{4}-2(-1.5)(1.5)+{1.5}^{2}-5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1.5 \\ 1.5\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-4.5 & 8.25 \\ -16.5 & 6\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3.875 \\ 6.8125\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1.5 \\ 1.5\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{-4.5\cdot 6-8.25\cdot (-16.5)}[\begin{aligned}6 & -8.25 \\ 16.5 & -4.5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3.875 \\ 6.8125\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1.5 \\ 1.5\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{109.125}[\begin{aligned}-32.953\,125 \\ 33.281\,250\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}-1.198 \\ 1.195\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to three decimal places.
